	rest pose. A play in place is then restored; a placed one stands again where it was placed.
	After.anyLanded(play): whether there is anything to fade or to return.

	Both return what Play:step returns: "active", "dormant" or "done".
]]

local Trajectory = require(script.Parent.Parent.Rocks.Trajectory)

local RESTING = 0
local LANDED = 2
local GONE = 3

local UP = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
local TINY = 1e-4
-- Fade: a piece ends this share of its thickness, and this many studs, under the surface.
local SINK_MARGIN_SHARE = 0.15
local SINK_MARGIN_STUDS = 0.1
-- Return: the share of the time spent flying the path backwards; the rest eases onto the rest pose.
local RETURN_PATH_SHARE = 0.85

local After = {}

-- How far a box of `halfExt`, turned as `frame`, reaches along a unit direction.
local function reachAlong(frame, halfExt, direction)
	return math.abs(frame.XVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.X
		+ math.abs(frame.YVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.Y
		+ math.abs(frame.ZVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.Z
end

-- How far a landed piece must sink along `normal` to be wholly under the surface it lies on.
function After.sinkDepth(frame, halfExt, normal)
	local thickness = 2 * reachAlong(frame, halfExt, normal)
	return thickness * (1 + SINK_MARGIN_SHARE) + SINK_MARGIN_STUDS
end

function After.anyLanded(play)
	for index in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] == LANDED then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

function After.fade(play, dt)
	play.phaseTime += dt
	local progress = math.clamp(play.phaseTime / math.max(play.settings.AfterTime, TINY), 0, 1)
	local sink = progress * progress
	local count = 0
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] == LANDED then
			local frame = play.lastFrame[index]
			local normal = play.path[index].restNormal or UP
			count += 1
			play.moveIndices[count] = index
			play.moveFrames[count] = frame + normal * (-After.sinkDepth(frame, piece.halfExt, normal) * sink)
		end
	end
	play:_flush(count)
	if progress < 1 then
		return "active"
	end
	for index in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] == LANDED then
			play.state[index] = GONE
			play.display.drop(index)
			play.awake -= 1
		end
	end
	play.phase = "live"
	return "dormant"
end

function After.back(play, dt)
	play.phaseTime += dt
	local progress = math.clamp(play.phaseTime / math.max(play.settings.AfterTime, TINY), 0, 1)
	local count = 0
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] == LANDED then
			local frame
			if progress < RETURN_PATH_SHARE then
				local remaining = 1 - progress / RETURN_PATH_SHARE
				frame = Trajectory.evaluate(play.path[index], play.landedAfter[index] * remaining, play.gravity[index])
			else
				local start = Trajectory.evaluate(play.path[index], 0, play.gravity[index])
				frame = start:Lerp(piece.rest, (progress - RETURN_PATH_SHARE) / (1 - RETURN_PATH_SHARE))
			end
			count += 1
			play.moveIndices[count] = index
			play.moveFrames[count] = frame
		end
	end
	play:_flush(count)
	if progress < 1 then
		return "active"
	end
	if not play.placed then
		play:restore()
		return "done"
	end
	-- A placed Reactor stands where it was placed again: the stand-ins stay, back at rest.
	for index in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] == LANDED then
			play.state[index] = RESTING
		end
	end
	play.phase = "live"
	play.phaseTime = 0
	play.idleFor = 0
	return "dormant"
end

return After

--[[
	Dice  -  cuts a box into smaller boxes that fill it exactly: the blocks a block-shaped part
	of a Reactor breaks into. Numbers only, no instances.

	Dice.cut(size, pieceSize, random) -> { { offset = Vector3, size = Vector3 }, ... }
	  size       the box's size
	  pieceSize  the edge a block should have, about; an edge of the box shorter than this is
	             not cut
	  random     a function giving 0 to 1; the same sequence gives the same blocks
	Each axis is cut by planes that run through the whole box, spaced evenly and then shifted a
	little, so the blocks are an uneven grid: every block touches its neighbours face to face and
	nothing overlaps or is left out. offset is a block's centre in the box's own space.
]]

local Dice = {}

-- A box is never cut into more blocks than this; a smaller Piece Size than that allows is
-- answered with fewer cuts along every axis.
Dice.MAX_BLOCKS = 240
-- How far a cut may be shifted from its even place, as a share of a block's length.
local SHIFT = 0.22
-- The smallest Piece Size that is taken at its word.
local LEAST_PIECE_SIZE = 0.25

-- The cut planes along one axis of `length`, from -length / 2 to length / 2, both ends included.
local function planes(length, count, random)
	local edges = table.create(count + 1)
	local step = length / count
	edges[1] = -length / 2
	for cut = 1, count - 1 do
		edges[cut + 1] = -length / 2 + step * (cut + (random() * 2 - 1) * SHIFT)
	end
	edges[count + 1] = length / 2
	return edges
end

function Dice.cut(size, pieceSize, random)
	local edge = math.max(pieceSize, LEAST_PIECE_SIZE)
	local countX = math.max(math.floor(size.X / edge + 0.5), 1)
	local countY = math.max(math.floor(size.Y / edge + 0.5), 1)
	local countZ = math.max(math.floor(size.Z / edge + 0.5), 1)
	while countX * countY * countZ > Dice.MAX_BLOCKS do
		local longest = math.max(countX, countY, countZ)
		if countX == longest then
			countX -= 1
		elseif countY == longest then
			countY -= 1
		else
			countZ -= 1
		end
	end

	local edgesX = planes(size.X, countX, random)
	local edgesY = planes(size.Y, countY, random)
	local edgesZ = planes(size.Z, countZ, random)
	local blocks = table.create(countX * countY * countZ)
	for x = 1, countX do
		for y = 1, countY do
			for z = 1, countZ do
				table.insert(blocks, {
					offset = Vector3.new((edgesX[x] + edgesX[x + 1]) / 2, (edgesY[y] + edgesY[y + 1]) / 2, (edgesZ[z] + edgesZ[z + 1]) / 2),
					size = Vector3.new(edgesX[x + 1] - edgesX[x], edgesY[y + 1] - edgesY[y], edgesZ[z + 1] - edgesZ[z]),
				})
			end
		end
	end
	return blocks
end

return Dice

--[[
	Display  -  what a Reactor's play looks like in the world: a stand-in for every piece that is
	out of place, and the original hidden while its stand-in exists. The four functions Reactor/Play
	calls (wake, move, drop, restore).

	A piece that is a block cut from a part (Reactor/Pieces, Break = "Blocks") gets a stand-in the
	size of the block, and the first block of a part to wake brings stand-ins for all its
	siblings with it: the part is hidden as a whole, so the blocks left standing must be shown.
	A piece that is a shard (Break = "Shards") gets a copy of its template (Reactor/Shards) in
	the part's look of that moment. A shard's template does not sit at the centre of the shard's
	box, which is what a piece's frame is: a shard's stand-in is placed at frame * standOffset.

	Only stand-ins ever move. They are copies that are not saved (Archivable off, under the
	runtime's folder, marked _PartIcleEmit so the start-up and shut-down sweeps remove strays).
	An original is LIVE user content and is written in one way only: hidden through
	LocalTransparencyModifier, which Roblox neither saves nor replicates, so a crash or a save
	in the middle of a play leaves the place as it was. A server has no such property to use:
	there the original's Transparency, CanCollide and CanQuery are set and put back from a copy
	of their values kept by this display.
]]

local EngineAttr = require(script.Parent.Parent.EngineAttr)
local Index = require(script.Parent.Index)

local CONFIG_NAME = "PartIcleProperties"

local Display = {}

-- Whether a stand-in takes a child of its original along: what draws on the part does. Parts
-- and anything that holds parts do not (they are pieces of their own, as Modules/Scatter's
-- field under a one-part Reactor), nor joints, values, code or the plugin's own children.
function Display.travels(child)
	if child:IsA("BasePart") or child:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("BasePart", true) then
		return false
	end
	if child:IsA("JointInstance") or child:IsA("Constraint") or child:IsA("WeldConstraint") or child:IsA("NoCollisionConstraint") then
		return false
	end
	if child:IsA("LuaSourceContainer") or child:IsA("ValueBase") then
		return false
	end
	if child.Name == CONFIG_NAME or child:GetAttribute("Transformed") then
		return false
	end
	return true
end

-- A shard's stand-in: a copy of its template, looking as the part does now.
local function makeShard(piece)
	local part = piece.part
	local copy = piece.shard:Clone()
	copy.Color = part.Color
	copy.Material = part.Material
	copy.MaterialVariant = part.MaterialVariant
	copy.Transparency = part.Transparency
	copy.Reflectance = part.Reflectance
	copy.Archivable = false
	copy.Anchored = true
	copy.CanCollide = false
	copy.CanQuery = false
	copy.CanTouch = false
	copy.Locked = true
	copy:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	return copy
end

local function makeStandIn(piece)
	if piece.shard then
		return makeShard(piece)
	end
	local part = piece.part
	local copy = Instance.fromExisting(part)
	copy.Archivable = false
	copy.Anchored = true
	copy.CanCollide = false
	copy.CanQuery = false
	copy.CanTouch = false
	copy.Locked = true
	-- A Reactor that is one part would hand its own marks to its stand-in.
	Index.unmark(copy)
	copy:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	if piece.blockSize then
		-- A block carries nothing over: what sat on the whole part's faces has no place on a cut of it.
		copy.Size = piece.blockSize
		return copy
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if Display.travels(child) then
			local childCopy = child:Clone()
			if childCopy then
				childCopy.Parent = copy
			end
		end
	end
	return copy
end

-- Hides or shows a LIVE original and the Decals and Textures directly on it.
local function setLocalHidden(part, hidden)
	local modifier = 0
	if hidden then
		modifier = 1
	end
	EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "LocalTransparencyModifier", modifier)
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("Decal") then
			EngineAttr.writeProp(child, "LocalTransparencyModifier", modifier)
		end
	end
end

-- pieces: Reactor/Pieces records. folder: where stand-ins live. onServer: true where there is
-- no local hide and the original's own properties are used.
function Display.new(pieces, folder, onServer)
	local standIns = {}
	-- part -> true while it is hidden, or (on a server) the values to put back.
	local hidden = {}
	local moveParts = {}
	local moveCount = 0
	local display = {}
	-- Only a display with shards rewrites the frames it is handed.
	local offsetFrames = nil
	for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		if piece.standOffset then
			offsetFrames = {}
			break
		end
	end

	-- Hides a LIVE original once, however many of its blocks ask.
	local function hideOriginal(part)
		if hidden[part] then
			return
		end
		if not onServer then
			hidden[part] = true
			setLocalHidden(part, true)
			return
		end
		hidden[part] = { Transparency = part.Transparency, CanCollide = part.CanCollide, CanQuery = part.CanQuery }
		EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "Transparency", 1)
		EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "CanCollide", false)
		EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "CanQuery", false)
	end

	local function showOriginal(part)
		local values = hidden[part]
		if not values then
			return
		end
		hidden[part] = nil
		if not part.Parent then
			return
		end
		if not onServer then
			setLocalHidden(part, false)
			return
		end
		EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "Transparency", values.Transparency)
		EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "CanCollide", values.CanCollide)
		EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "CanQuery", values.CanQuery)
	end

	local function place(index)
		local piece = pieces[index]
		local copy = makeStandIn(piece)
		if piece.standOffset then
			copy.CFrame = piece.rest * piece.standOffset
		else
			copy.CFrame = piece.rest
		end
		copy.Parent = folder
		standIns[index] = copy
	end

	-- Returns how many stand-ins it made, which is what a frame's wake budget counts.
	function display.wake(index)
		local piece = pieces[index]
		local made = 0
		if piece.siblings then
			for _, sibling in ipairs(piece.siblings) do
				if not standIns[sibling] then
					place(sibling)
					made += 1
				end
			end
		elseif not standIns[index] then
			place(index)
			made = 1
		end
		hideOriginal(piece.part)
		return made
	end

	-- Every index must have its stand-in: BulkMoveTo takes a missing one as the end of the list
	-- and refuses the move. Reactor/Play drops a lost piece before it lists the frame's moves.
	function display.move(indices, frames, count)
		for position = 1, count do
			moveParts[position] = standIns[indices[position]]
		end
		for position = count + 1, moveCount do
			moveParts[position] = nil
		end
		if offsetFrames then
			for position = 1, count do
				local standOffset = pieces[indices[position]].standOffset
				if standOffset then
					offsetFrames[position] = frames[position] * standOffset
				else
					offsetFrames[position] = frames[position]
				end
			end
			for position = count + 1, moveCount do
				offsetFrames[position] = nil
			end
			frames = offsetFrames
		end
		moveCount = count
		workspace:BulkMoveTo(moveParts, frames, Enum.BulkMoveMode.FireCFrameChanged)
	end

	function display.drop(index)
		local copy = standIns[index]
		if copy then
			copy:Destroy()
			standIns[index] = nil
		end
	end

	-- A block takes its siblings with it: the part comes back whole or not at all.
	function display.restore(index)
		local piece = pieces[index]
		if piece.siblings then
			for _, sibling in ipairs(piece.siblings) do
				display.drop(sibling)
			end
		else
			display.drop(index)
		end
		showOriginal(piece.part)
	end

	-- The original of a piece, for whoever must leave it out of a ray.
	function display.original(index)
		return pieces[index].part
	end

	return display
end

return Display

--[[
	Driven  -  the pieces of a play that a Continuous Force is carrying (wind, a tornado, a pull).
	Part of Reactor/Play, split out for size: it reads and writes the play's own tables.

	A Continuous Force is a flow: its Strength is the speed, in studs per second, it carries a
	piece at, along the direction Force/Fields gives. A carried piece takes up that speed within
	a fraction of a second (GRIP). Gravity still holds it down unless the flow rises: a wind along
	the ground rolls pieces over it, while a rising flow carries a piece up at the flow's own
	speed, slower where the Force has faded, until the piece leaves the shape and falls.
	Each piece is stepped live, one floor ray and one wall ray a step, only while a Force holds
	it; when none does it is put back on a built path (Play:_launch) and lands like any other.

	capture(play, record) takes in the pieces a Continuous record has reached.
	step(play, dt, count) advances every driven piece and adds its pose to the play's move lists
	from position count + 1; returns the new count.
]]

local Fields = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Fields)
local Trajectory = require(script.Parent.Parent.Rocks.Trajectory)

local RESTING = 0
local FLYING = 1
local LANDED = 2
local GONE = 3
local DRIVEN = 4

local ZERO = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)
local TINY = 1e-4
-- Steps of at most this long, and no more than a few a frame.
local STEP_SECONDS = 1 / 60
local MAX_STEPS = 3
-- How fast a piece takes up the Force's speed, per second.
local GRIP = 6
-- How far below a piece the floor ray looks beyond the piece's own half height.
local FLOOR_MARGIN = 0.1
-- A flow whose upward part is at least this share of its speed spares a piece gravity
-- altogether; a level flow spares none.
local LIFTING_SHARE = 0.25
-- Turbulence: how fast the gusts change, and how far apart two pieces' gusts are.
local GUST_RATE = 1.7
local GUST_SPREAD = 0.37

local Driven = {}

Driven.STATE = DRIVEN

-- How far a turned box reaches along a unit direction.
local function support(rotation, halfExt, direction)
	return math.abs(rotation.XVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.X
		+ math.abs(rotation.YVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.Y
		+ math.abs(rotation.ZVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.Z
end

-- What the Continuous Forces of a play ask of a piece at `position`: the velocity to carry it
-- at, the share of gravity it is spared (0 for a level flow, 1 for one that rises), and whether
-- any Force holds it at all.
local function flowAt(play, index, position)
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	local velocity = ZERO
	local held = false
	for record in pairs(play.kicks) do
		if record.actsAs == "Continuous" and not record.ended then
			local strength = record.strength
			local direction, distance, distance01 = Fields.sample(record.field, position, strength < 0)
			if direction and distance <= record.front then
				local share = Fields.kept(record.falloff, distance01) * Fields.sizeShare(piece.size, record.sizeResponse)
				local gust = 1
				if record.turbulence > 0 then
					gust = 1 + record.turbulence * 2 * math.noise(play.clock * GUST_RATE, index * GUST_SPREAD, record.seed * 10)
				end
				velocity += direction * (math.abs(strength) * share * gust)
				held = true
			end
		end
	end
	local speed = velocity.Magnitude
	local rising = 0
	if speed > TINY then
		rising = math.clamp(velocity.Y / (speed * LIFTING_SHARE), 0, 1)
	end
	return velocity, rising, held
end

-- Takes a piece that is out of place off its path and into the flow, from where it is.
local function enter(play, index)
	local elapsed = play.clock - play.pathStart[index]
	local gravity = play.gravity[index]
	local frame = Trajectory.evaluate(play.path[index], elapsed, gravity)
	local velocity, spin = Trajectory.velocity(play.path[index], elapsed, gravity)
	if spin.Magnitude < TINY then
		spin = play.path[index].segs[1].w
	end
	play.drivePosition[index] = frame.Position
	play.driveRotation[index] = frame.Rotation
	play.driveVelocity[index] = velocity
	play.driveSpin[index] = spin
	play.state[index] = DRIVEN
	table.insert(play.driven, index)
end

-- The pieces a Continuous record has reached: a resting one is woken (it joins the flow on a
-- later frame, once it has its stand-in), one already out of place joins now. A Force that
-- would carry a piece no faster than Hold leaves it be.
function Driven.capture(play, record)
	local strength = record.strength
	local pulls = strength < 0
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		local state = play.state[index]
		if state ~= DRIVEN and state ~= GONE then
			local direction, distance, distance01 = Fields.sample(record.field, play:_position(index), pulls)
			if direction and distance <= record.front then
				local speed = math.abs(strength) * Fields.kept(record.falloff, distance01) * Fields.sizeShare(piece.size, record.sizeResponse)
				if speed > play:_holdOf(index) then
					if state == RESTING then
						play:_push(index, ZERO)
					elseif state == FLYING or state == LANDED then
						enter(play, index)
					end
					play:_takeTime(record)
				end
			end
		end
	end
end

-- One step of one piece. Returns its new position, velocity and rotation.
local function advance(play, index, position, velocity, rotation, flow, spared, stepSeconds)
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	local gravity = play.gravity[index]
	velocity += (flow - velocity) * math.min(GRIP * stepSeconds, 1)
	velocity += Vector3.new(0, -gravity * (1 - spared) * stepSeconds, 0)
	local move = velocity * stepSeconds

	-- Walls: what lies ahead along the level part of the move.
	local level = Vector3.new(move.X, 0, move.Z)
	local levelDistance = level.Magnitude
	if levelDistance > TINY then
		local ahead = level / levelDistance
		local wall = play.castRay(position, ahead * (levelDistance + support(rotation, piece.halfExt, ahead)))
		if wall then
			local into = move:Dot(wall.Normal)
			if into < 0 then
				move -= wall.Normal * into
			end
			local speedInto = velocity:Dot(wall.Normal)
			if speedInto < 0 then
				velocity -= wall.Normal * speedInto
			end
		end
	end

	-- Floor: the piece may not sink below its own half height above what is under it.
	local halfHeight = support(rotation, piece.halfExt, Vector3.new(0, 1, 0))
	local floor = play.castRay(position, Vector3.new(0, -(halfHeight + math.max(-move.Y, 0) + FLOOR_MARGIN), 0))
	if floor then
		local lowest = floor.Position.Y + halfHeight
		if position.Y + move.Y < lowest then
			move = Vector3.new(move.X, lowest - position.Y, move.Z)
			if velocity.Y < 0 then
				velocity = Vector3.new(velocity.X, 0, velocity.Z)
			end
		end
	end

	local spin = play.driveSpin[index]
	local turn = spin.Magnitude
	if turn * stepSeconds > TINY then
		rotation = CFrame.fromAxisAngle(spin / turn, turn * stepSeconds) * rotation
	end
	return position + move, velocity, rotation
end

function Driven.step(play, dt, count)
	local driven = play.driven
	if #driven == 0 or dt <= 0 then
		return count
	end
	local steps = math.clamp(math.ceil(dt / STEP_SECONDS), 1, MAX_STEPS)
	local stepSeconds = dt / steps
	local place = 1
	while place <= #driven do
		local index = driven[place]
		local position = play.drivePosition[index]
		local velocity = play.driveVelocity[index]
		local rotation = play.driveRotation[index]
		local held = true
		for _ = 1, steps do
			local flow, spared, inside = flowAt(play, index, position)
			if not inside then
				held = false
				break
			end
			position, velocity, rotation = advance(play, index, position, velocity, rotation, flow, spared, stepSeconds)
		end

		local frame = rotation + position
		play.lastFrame[index] = frame
		if held then
			play.drivePosition[index] = position
			play.driveVelocity[index] = velocity
			play.driveRotation[index] = rotation
			count += 1
			play.moveIndices[count] = index
			play.moveFrames[count] = frame
			place += 1
		else
			-- No Force holds it any more: back onto a built path, from here, at this speed.
			local last = #driven
			driven[place] = driven[last]
			driven[last] = nil
			play.state[index] = LANDED
			play:_launch(index, frame, velocity, play.driveSpin[index])
		end
	end
	return count
end

return Driven

--[[
	Index  -  which Reactors a Force could reach. A Reactor is found by its tag (set by
	TransformReactor), so nothing is scanned: a place with no Reactors costs one empty list.
	Index.reaches is a first, generous test (a ball around the Reactor against a ball around
	the Force's shape); Reactor/Play decides piece by piece.
	Index.unmark makes a copy of a Reactor an ordinary instance again (Reactor/Display's
	stand-ins, the plugin's Modules/Scatter).
]]

local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")

local Index = {}

Index.TAG = "PartIcleReactor"
-- The item attributes TransformReactor (Reactor/init.luau) stamps; one added there is added here.
Index.MARKS = { "Transformed", "Qwinkle", "IsReactor", "IsEmitter", "EmitCount", "EmitDuration", "EmitDelay", "EmissionMode", "AnimateLoop" }

-- Every tagged Reactor that is in the world right now.
function Index.reactors()
	local found = {}
	for _, reactor in ipairs(CollectionService:GetTagged(Index.TAG)) do
		if reactor:IsDescendantOf(workspace) and not reactor:GetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit") then
			table.insert(found, reactor)
		end
	end
	return found
end

-- The farthest any point of a field's shape is from its origin.
function Index.reachOf(field)
	if field.shape == "Linear" then
		return math.sqrt(field.range * field.range + field.halfWidth * field.halfWidth + field.halfHeight * field.halfHeight)
	elseif field.shape == "Vortex" then
		return math.sqrt(field.range * field.range + field.height * field.height)
	end
	return field.range
end

function Index.reaches(field, centre, radius)
	return (centre - field.origin.Position).Magnitude <= radius + Index.reachOf(field)
end

-- Takes a Reactor's attributes and tag off a COPY of one. Never called on the Reactor itself.
function Index.unmark(copy)
	for _, mark in ipairs(Index.MARKS) do
		copy:SetAttribute(mark, nil)
	end
	copy:RemoveTag(Index.TAG)
end

-- A Force's Group reaches a Reactor when it is empty or the same.
function Index.groupMatches(forceGroup, reactorGroup)
	return forceGroup == "" or forceGroup == reactorGroup
end

return Index

--[[
	Pieces  -  the parts of a Reactor that can be pushed, as records for Reactor/Play:
	{ part, rest (its CFrame now), halfExt, size, reach }.
	A Model has every BasePart under it; a Reactor that is one part has itself and every
	BasePart under it (Modules/Scatter places copies there). A transformed item inside (an
	emitter with its own RenderTemplate) keeps to itself and is skipped with everything under
	it. Read each time a play starts, so hand edits are picked up.

	With Break = "Blocks" a plain block-shaped Part gives one record per block it is cut into
	(Reactor/Dice): the same part, blockSize (the block's own size), and siblings, one list shared
	by all the blocks of that part, holding their places in the returned array. Any other part
	(a wedge, a cylinder, a mesh, a union, a Part carrying a mesh) stays one piece.
	The cut is the same every time for the same Reactor: each part draws from its own seed.

	With Break = "Shards" a part gives one record per shard the caller has for it:
	shardsOf(part) -> { { template, box, size, standOffset }, ... } (Reactor/Shards) or nil for a
	part that moves whole. A record's rest is the shard's own box, in the world; it carries
	shard (the template its stand-in is copied from), standOffset and siblings as a block does.

	Pieces.parts(reactor) -> the parts collect reads, in its order: the Reactor itself when it
	is a part, then every BasePart under it outside transformed items.

	Pieces.carry(pieces, own, origin, fullPose) moves the records of a Reactor that is emitted
	somewhere else (EmitAt, an event) to that place: the parts themselves stay where they are.
]]

local Dice = require(script.Parent.Dice)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)

local Pieces = {}

-- size: the edge of a cube of the volume, what a Force's Size Response goes by.
-- reach: the longest edge.
local function record(part, rest, size)
	return {
		part = part,
		rest = rest,
		halfExt = size / 2,
		size = (size.X * size.Y * size.Z) ^ (1 / 3),
		reach = math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z),
	}
end

-- A plain box: a Part whose Shape is Block and that carries no mesh of its own.
local function isPlainBlock(part)
	if part.ClassName ~= "Part" or part.Shape ~= Enum.PartType.Block then
		return false
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("DataModelMesh") then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

-- One record per shard of a part, or false when the caller has none for it.
local function addShards(pieces, part, shardsOf)
	local shards = shardsOf and shardsOf(part) or nil
	if not shards or #shards < 2 then
		return false
	end
	local siblings = table.create(#shards)
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
		local piece = record(part, part.CFrame * shard.box, shard.size)
		piece.shard = shard.template
		piece.standOffset = shard.standOffset
		piece.siblings = siblings
		table.insert(pieces, piece)
		table.insert(siblings, #pieces)
	end
	return true
end

local function add(pieces, part, breakMode, pieceSize, shardsOf)
	if breakMode == "Shards" and addShards(pieces, part, shardsOf) then
		return
	end
	if breakMode ~= "Blocks" or not isPlainBlock(part) then
		table.insert(pieces, record(part, part.CFrame, part.Size))
		return
	end
	local blocks = Dice.cut(part.Size, pieceSize, Sites.sequence(#pieces * 7919 + 13))
	if #blocks == 1 then
		table.insert(pieces, record(part, part.CFrame, part.Size))
		return
	end
	local siblings = table.create(#blocks)
	for _, block in ipairs(blocks) do
		local piece = record(part, part.CFrame * CFrame.new(block.offset.X, block.offset.Y, block.offset.Z), block.size)
		piece.blockSize = block.size
		piece.siblings = siblings
		table.insert(pieces, piece)
		table.insert(siblings, #pieces)
	end
end

local function visit(parent, parts)
	for _, child in ipairs(parent:GetChildren()) do
		if not child:GetAttribute("Transformed") then
			if child:IsA("BasePart") and not child:IsA("Terrain") then
				table.insert(parts, child)
			end
			visit(child, parts)
		end
	end
end

function Pieces.parts(reactor)
	local parts = {}
	if reactor:IsA("BasePart") then
		table.insert(parts, reactor)
	end
	visit(reactor, parts)
	return parts
end

-- Rewrites every rest pose for a Reactor whose frame is `own` and that is emitted at `origin`.
-- A full pose brings the layout into the origin's frame; otherwise it is only moved there and
-- every piece keeps its rotation.
function Pieces.carry(pieces, own, origin, fullPose)
	if fullPose then
		for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
			piece.rest = origin * own:ToObjectSpace(piece.rest)
		end
		return
	end
	local shift = origin.Position - own.Position
	for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		piece.rest = piece.rest + shift
	end
end

function Pieces.collect(reactor, breakMode, pieceSize, shardsOf)
	local pieces = {}
	for _, part in ipairs(Pieces.parts(reactor)) do
		add(pieces, part, breakMode, pieceSize or 2, shardsOf)
	end
	return pieces
end

return Pieces

--[[
	Play  -  one disturbed Reactor: which pieces are out of place, on what paths, and what happens
	once they have all come to rest (the Fade and the Return are Reactor/After). Logic only: instances are reached through `display`
	(Reactor/Display in the runtime, a recorder in the tests) and the world through `castRay`, so
	all of it runs under the luau CLI.

	A piece is { rest = CFrame, halfExt = Vector3, size = number, reach = number }.
	States: RESTING (never pushed: the original stands, the play shows nothing for it), FLYING
	(on a path), LANDED (its path ended; it lies where it fell), GONE (sunk away or lost), DRIVEN
	(carried by a Continuous Force: Reactor/Driven steps it live until no Force holds it).

	A pushed piece flies a path from Rocks/Trajectory: a plain arc at once, replaced by the whole
	built path (bounces, roll-out, rest pose) within the per-frame build budget. A push on a piece
	already out of place rebuilds its path from where it is and how fast it goes.

	A Force's strength is a distance: how far, in studs, it throws a piece (Fields.throwSpeed
	turns it into a speed under the piece's own gravity). Hold is a distance too: a throw no
	longer than Hold leaves the piece standing.

	With settings.Collapse, a piece left standing with no chain of standing neighbours to
	something that carries it (Reactor/Support) is let go and falls. The graph is built the first
	time a piece of the play wakes.

	settings: Hold, HoldSpread, Collapse, isAnchored(index) (asked once per piece when Collapse
	is on), After ("Stay" | "Fade" | "Return"), AfterDelay, AfterTime,
	MaxPieces, MaxAirTime (seconds a piece may fly: its path looks for ground that long, and
	one still in the air after it is taken away; never less than a second),
	wakeBudget (stand-ins made per frame), buildBudget (paths built per frame), and
	the functions rollGravity(),
	rollBounciness(), rollFriction(), rollTumble() (radians per second) and random() (0 to 1).
	display: wake(index) shows a stand-in for a piece, hides the original and returns how many
	stand-ins it made (a block brings its siblings); move(indices, frames, count) places stand-ins; drop(index) removes one for good; restore(index) removes it
	and shows the original again.

	A play can be placed (Play:place): every piece is given its stand-in at once and stands at
	rest, for a Reactor emitted somewhere other than where its parts are. Nothing moves until a
	Force pushes; a pushed piece then goes at once, its stand-in being there already, and a
	Return ends with the Reactor standing at that place again.

	step(dt) returns "active" while anything moves or is still to come, "dormant" when the pieces
	lie where they fell and nothing more happens without a new Force, and "done" when every piece
	is back at rest and the play can be thrown away.
]]

local Trajectory = require(script.Parent.Parent.Rocks.Trajectory)
local Fields = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Fields)
local Driven = require(script.Parent.Driven)
local Support = require(script.Parent.Support)
local After = require(script.Parent.After)

local RESTING = 0
local FLYING = 1
local LANDED = 2
local GONE = 3
local DRIVEN = Driven.STATE

local ZERO = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)
local UP = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
local TINY = 1e-4
-- The least a play's Max Air Time counts as.
local LEAST_AIR_TIME = 1
-- How far above a surface a piece buried past its middle starts its flight.
local SURFACE_MARGIN = 0.02

local Play = {}
Play.__index = Play

function Play.new(pieces, settings, display, castRay)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Play)
	self.pieces = pieces
	self.settings = settings
	self.display = display
	self.castRay = castRay
	-- A piece whose built path meets no ground within this many seconds is taken away then.
	self.airTime = math.max(settings.MaxAirTime, LEAST_AIR_TIME)
	-- Rocks/Trajectory.build's rules for a piece: it leaves walls, it starts where it stood, on
	-- the ground or sunk into it, which a Rocks chunk does not, and ground is looked for all
	-- through its air time.
	self.pathRules = { offWalls = true, fromRest = true, airTime = self.airTime }
	self.clock = 0
	self.state = table.create(#pieces, RESTING)
	-- Per piece, set at its first launch.
	self.path = {}
	self.pathStart = {}
	self.pathBuilt = {}
	self.gravity = {}
	self.bounciness = {}
	self.friction = {}
	self.lastFrame = {}
	self.landedAfter = {}
	self.holdOf = {}
	-- Reactor/Support's graph, and whether pieces have left since it was last walked.
	self.support = nil
	self.supportStale = false
	-- record -> the pieces it has already reached.
	self.kicks = {}
	self.flying = {}
	-- The pieces a Continuous Force carries, and their live state (Reactor/Driven).
	self.driven = {}
	self.drivePosition = {}
	self.driveRotation = {}
	self.driveVelocity = {}
	self.driveSpin = {}
	self.pendingWake = {}
	self.pendingPush = {}
	self.buildQueue = {}
	self.moveIndices = {}
	self.moveFrames = {}
	self.moveCount = 0
	-- Pieces with a stand-in, and pieces whose original is hidden (a faded piece is still hidden).
	self.awake = 0
	self.hidden = 0
	-- True once Play:place has stood every piece up as a stand-in.
	self.placed = false
	self.phase = "live"
	self.phaseTime = 0
	self.idleFor = 0
	-- The time sources of the Forces that have moved a piece of this play (Force/Registry:
	-- record.time, a Container's, and record.ownTime, the Force's own Timescale). Reactor/init
	-- steps the play by the slowest of them.
	self.times = {}
	return self
end

-- Starts following a Force. False while the play is fading or returning: those finish first.
function Play:watch(record)
	if self.phase ~= "live" then
		return false
	end
	if not self.kicks[record] then
		self.kicks[record] = {}
	end
	self.idleFor = 0
	return true
end

-- The kick of an Impulse that arrived before this play existed, given NOW: a Reactor whose
-- shards were still being cut (Reactor/init) answers late. An Impulse lasts a frame or two, so
-- one that is merely followed can be over before this play's first step and its kick lost.
-- One still alive is followed as well, and remembers the pieces it has kicked here.
function Play:strike(record)
	if self.phase ~= "live" then
		return false
	end
	local kicked = {}
	if not record.ended and self:watch(record) then
		kicked = self.kicks[record]
	end
	self:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
	self.idleFor = 0
	return true
end

-- A Force that moves a piece of this play lends the play its time. Following one is not
-- enough: a play out of place follows every Force of its Group, however far away.
function Play:_takeTime(record)
	local times = self.times
	local carried = record.time
	if carried and not table.find(times, carried) then
		table.insert(times, carried)
	end
	local own = record.ownTime
	if own and not table.find(times, own) then
		table.insert(times, own)
	end
end

function Play:_position(index)
	if self.state[index] == RESTING then
		return self.pieces[index].rest.Position
	end
	return self.lastFrame[index].Position
end

local function randomAxis(random)
	local axis = Vector3.new(random() * 2 - 1, random() * 2 - 1, random() * 2 - 1)
	if axis.Magnitude < TINY then
		return UP
	end
	return axis.Unit
end

-- A piece's own Hold: the Reactor's, spread by HoldSpread, rolled the first time it is asked for.
function Play:_holdOf(index)
	local hold = self.holdOf[index]
	if hold == nil then
		local settings = self.settings
		hold = settings.Hold * (1 + settings.HoldSpread * (settings.random() * 2 - 1))
		self.holdOf[index] = hold
	end
	return hold
end

-- A piece's own gravity, bounciness and friction, rolled the first time they are asked for.
function Play:_rolled(index)
	local settings = self.settings
	if self.gravity[index] == nil then
		self.gravity[index] = settings.rollGravity()
		self.bounciness[index] = settings.rollBounciness()
		self.friction[index] = settings.rollFriction()
	end
	return self.gravity[index]
end

-- Puts a piece on a plain arc from `frame` and queues the whole path for building.
function Play:_launch(index, frame, velocity, spin)
	local settings = self.settings
	self:_rolled(index)
	if spin.Magnitude < TINY then
		spin = randomAxis(settings.random) * settings.rollTumble()
	end
	self.path[index] = Trajectory.ballistic(frame.Position, velocity, frame.Rotation, spin)
	self.pathStart[index] = self.clock
	self.pathBuilt[index] = false
	self.lastFrame[index] = frame
	table.insert(self.buildQueue, index)
	if self.state[index] ~= FLYING then
		self.state[index] = FLYING
		table.insert(self.flying, index)
	end
end

-- Where a resting piece starts its flight. One buried past its middle starts just above the
-- surface it lies in: a ray cast from inside the ground does not find it.
function Play:_surfaced(index)
	local piece = self.pieces[index]
	local rest = piece.rest
	local reach = Support.worldHalf(piece).Y + SURFACE_MARGIN
	local over = self.castRay(rest.Position + UP * reach, UP * -reach)
	if not over then
		return rest
	end
	return rest + UP * (over.Position.Y - rest.Position.Y + SURFACE_MARGIN)
end

-- A push on one piece. A resting piece waits for its stand-in; a moving one is re-launched now.
function Play:_push(index, push)
	local state = self.state[index]
	if state == GONE then
		return
	end
	if state == RESTING then
		if self.placed then
			-- Its stand-in stands there already: it goes now, and counts against no cap.
			self:_launch(index, self:_surfaced(index), push, ZERO)
			self.supportStale = true
			return
		end
		if self.pendingPush[index] then
			self.pendingPush[index] += push
			return
		end
		if self.awake + #self.pendingWake >= self.settings.MaxPieces then
			return
		end
		self.pendingPush[index] = push
		table.insert(self.pendingWake, index)
		return
	end
	if state == DRIVEN then
		self.driveVelocity[index] += push
		return
	end
	local elapsed = self.clock - self.pathStart[index]
	local gravity = self.gravity[index]
	local frame = Trajectory.evaluate(self.path[index], elapsed, gravity)
	local velocity, spin = Trajectory.velocity(self.path[index], elapsed, gravity)
	self:_launch(index, frame, velocity + push, spin)
end

-- One kick for every piece the front of an Impulse has reached since the last frame.
function Play:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
	local settings = self.settings
	local field = record.field
	local front = record.front
	local strength = record.strength
	local pulls = strength < 0
	for index, piece in ipairs(self.pieces) do
		if not kicked[index] and self.state[index] ~= GONE then
			local direction, distance, distance01 = Fields.sample(field, self:_position(index), pulls)
			if direction and distance <= front then
				kicked[index] = true
				local share = Fields.sizeShare(piece.size, record.sizeResponse)
				local spread = 1 + record.variation * (settings.random() * 2 - 1)
				local throw = strength * Fields.kept(record.falloff, distance01) * share * spread
				if math.abs(throw) > self:_holdOf(index) then
					self:_push(index, direction * Fields.throwSpeed(throw, self:_rolled(index)))
					self:_takeTime(record)
				end
			end
		end
	end
end

function Play:_followForces()
	for record, kicked in pairs(self.kicks) do
		if record.ended then
			self.kicks[record] = nil
		elseif record.actsAs == "Impulse" then
			self:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
		else
			Driven.capture(self, record)
		end
	end
end

-- Stand-ins for the pieces waiting to move, until the frame's budget of new stand-ins is spent.
function Play:_wakePending()
	local pending = self.pendingWake
	local budget = self.settings.wakeBudget
	local taken = 0
	local made = 0
	while taken < #pending and made < budget do
		taken += 1
		local index = pending[taken]
		local push = self.pendingPush[index]
		self.pendingPush[index] = nil
		made += self.display.wake(index) or 1
		self.awake += 1
		self.hidden += 1
		self:_launch(index, self:_surfaced(index), push, ZERO)
	end
	if taken == 0 then
		return
	end
	self.supportStale = true
	local remaining = {}
	for position = taken + 1, #pending do
		table.insert(remaining, pending[position])
	end
	self.pendingWake = remaining
end

-- Lets go of every standing piece that has lost its last chain to something that carries it.
-- Those wake over the next frames like any other, and may bring more down in their turn.
function Play:_collapse()
	self.supportStale = false
	local settings = self.settings
	if not settings.Collapse then
		return
	end
	if not self.support then
		self.support = Support.build(self.pieces, settings.isAnchored)
	end
	local fallen = Support.unsupported(self.support, function(index)
		return self.state[index] == RESTING and self.pendingPush[index] == nil
	end)
	for _, index in ipairs(fallen) do
		self:_push(index, ZERO)
	end
end

-- Whole paths in place of plain arcs, as many as the frame's budget allows.
function Play:_buildPaths()
	local queue = self.buildQueue
	local taken = math.min(#queue, self.settings.buildBudget)
	if taken == 0 then
		return
	end
	for position = 1, taken do
		local index = queue[position]
		if self.state[index] == FLYING and not self.pathBuilt[index] then
			local start = self.path[index].segs[1]
			self.path[index] = Trajectory.build(start.p0, start.v0, start.rot0, start.w, self.pieces[index].halfExt, 1,
				self.gravity[index], self.bounciness[index], self.friction[index], self.castRay, self.pathRules)
			self.pathBuilt[index] = true
		end
	end
	local remaining = {}
	for position = taken + 1, #queue do
		table.insert(remaining, queue[position])
	end
	self.buildQueue = remaining
end

-- The poses of this frame are gathered in the move lists (flying pieces, then driven ones) and
-- handed to the display in one go. The lists are cut to `count`: a display may pass
-- them straight to BulkMoveTo.
function Play:_flush(count)
	local indices = self.moveIndices
	local frames = self.moveFrames
	for position = count + 1, self.moveCount do
		indices[position] = nil
		frames[position] = nil
	end
	self.moveCount = count
	if count > 0 then
		self.display.move(indices, frames, count)
	end
end

-- Returns how many poses it put in the move lists.
function Play:_moveFlying()
	local flying = self.flying
	local count = 0
	local position = 1
	while position <= #flying do
		local index = flying[position]
		-- A piece a Continuous Force took over is dropped from the list here.
		if self.state[index] ~= FLYING then
			local last = #flying
			flying[position] = flying[last]
			flying[last] = nil
			continue
		end
		local path = self.path[index]
		local elapsed = self.clock - self.pathStart[index]
		-- A lost piece leaves before it is listed: the display moves every piece it is handed,
		-- and one whose stand-in is gone stops the whole move (Reactor/Display.move).
		if self.pathBuilt[index] and path.restT == math.huge and elapsed > self.airTime then
			local last = #flying
			flying[position] = flying[last]
			flying[last] = nil
			self.state[index] = GONE
			self.display.drop(index)
			self.awake -= 1
			continue
		end
		local frame = Trajectory.evaluate(path, elapsed, self.gravity[index])
		self.lastFrame[index] = frame
		count += 1
		self.moveIndices[count] = index
		self.moveFrames[count] = frame

		if self.pathBuilt[index] and elapsed >= path.restT then
			local last = #flying
			flying[position] = flying[last]
			flying[last] = nil
			self.state[index] = LANDED
			self.landedAfter[index] = path.restT
		else
			position += 1
		end
	end
	return count
end

function Play:step(dt)
	self.clock += dt
	if self.phase == "fading" then
		return After.fade(self, dt)
	elseif self.phase == "returning" then
		return After.back(self, dt)
	end

	self:_followForces()
	self:_wakePending()
	if self.supportStale then
		self:_collapse()
	end
	self:_buildPaths()
	self:_flush(Driven.step(self, dt, self:_moveFlying()))

	if #self.flying > 0 or #self.driven > 0 or #self.pendingWake > 0 or next(self.kicks) ~= nil then
		self.idleFor = 0
		return "active"
	end
	if self.hidden == 0 then
		return "done"
	end
	local after = self.settings.After
	if after == "Stay" or self.awake == 0 or not After.anyLanded(self) then
		return "dormant"
	end
	self.idleFor += dt
	if self.idleFor >= self.settings.AfterDelay then
		self.phaseTime = 0
		if after == "Fade" then
			self.phase = "fading"
		else
			self.phase = "returning"
		end
	end
	return "active"
end

-- Stands the whole Reactor up as stand-ins, the originals hidden: for a play whose rest poses
-- are somewhere other than the parts (Reactor/Pieces.carry). Nothing is let go: a piece stays
-- where it stands until a Force pushes it or it loses its support. Called once, on a new play.
function Play:place()
	if self.placed then
		return
	end
	self.placed = true
	for index in ipairs(self.pieces) do
		self.display.wake(index)
		self.awake += 1
		self.hidden += 1
	end
end

-- Everything back: stand-ins removed, originals shown, the play as new.
function Play:restore()
	for index in ipairs(self.pieces) do
		if self.state[index] ~= RESTING or self.placed then
			self.display.restore(index)
			self.state[index] = RESTING
		end
	end
	self.placed = false
	self.flying = {}
	self.driven = {}
	self.pendingWake = {}
	self.pendingPush = {}
	self.buildQueue = {}
	self.kicks = {}
	self:_flush(0)
	self.awake = 0
	self.hidden = 0
	self.phase = "live"
	self.phaseTime = 0
	self.idleFor = 0
end

Play.RESTING = RESTING
Play.FLYING = FLYING
Play.LANDED = LANDED
Play.GONE = GONE
Play.DRIVEN = DRIVEN

return Play

--[[
	Shards  -  what a part breaks into with Break = "Shards": real fragments, cut by the engine
	(GeometryService:FragmentAsync) around points of ours (Reactor/Sites) and kept OUT of the
	world as templates. Reactor/Display copies its stand-ins from them; the part itself is read
	and never changed.

	The cut yields (about 30 ms for 50 shards of a plain part, measured in Studio), and a play
	needs its pieces up front. So shards are cut ahead and kept per part under a key that names
	everything the cut depends on; Reactor/init asks for them and, when they are not there yet,
	has them cut and lets the Reactor answer its Force a few frames late.

	Shards.cuttable(part) -> boolean      a Part, wedge, MeshPart or union that draws its own
	                                      shape; a Part carrying a mesh, a truss and Terrain are not
	Shards.key(part, count, seed, hit) -> string
	Shards.get(part, key) -> shards | false | nil
	    shards: { { template, box, size, standOffset }, ... }
	        template     the fragment, a MeshPart with no parent
	        box          the shard's own box as a frame in the PART's space; size its extents
	        standOffset  where the template sits in that box's frame: a stand-in at frame F of
	                     the piece has CFrame F * standOffset
	    false: the engine refused the part, or gave fewer than two shards; it moves whole.
	    nil: not cut under that key yet.
	Shards.prepare(jobs, done)
	    jobs: { { part, key, count, seed, hit }, ... }. Cuts them, a few at a time, and calls
	    done() once all are kept. Returns at once.

	Kept sets are held by the part alone (weak keys): they go when the part does, and a part
	cut again under another key drops its old set. Nothing here is saved with the place: the
	engine does not keep fragments across sessions, so they are cut again in each.
]]

local GeometryService = game:GetService("GeometryService")
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)

-- Cuts running at once.
local WORKERS = 4
-- A hit is the same hit within this many studs: the key rounds to it.
local HIT_STEP = 0.5

local Shards = {}

-- part -> { key = string, shards = table or false }
local kept = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

function Shards.cuttable(part)
	if part:IsA("MeshPart") or part:IsA("PartOperation") then
		return true
	end
	if part:IsA("Part") or part:IsA("WedgePart") or part:IsA("CornerWedgePart") then
		-- A Part that carries a mesh draws the mesh, which is not what the engine would cut.
		return part:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("DataModelMesh") == nil
	end
	return false
end

function Shards.key(part, count, seed, hit)
	local size = part.Size
	local shape = part.ClassName
	if part:IsA("MeshPart") then
		shape ..= part.MeshId
	elseif part:IsA("Part") then
		shape ..= part.Shape.Name
	end
	local where = "even"
	if hit then
		where = string.format("%d,%d,%d", math.round(hit.X / HIT_STEP), math.round(hit.Y / HIT_STEP), math.round(hit.Z / HIT_STEP))
	end
	return string.format("%s|%.3f,%.3f,%.3f|%d|%d|%s", shape, size.X, size.Y, size.Z, count, seed, where)
end

function Shards.get(part, key)
	local set = kept[part]
	if set and set.key == key then
		return set.shards
	end
	return nil
end

-- The engine's fragments of `part` around world points, or nil. Yields. A wedge is refused as
-- it is and accepted as a union of itself alone.
local function fragment(part, points)
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:FragmentAsync(part, points)
	end)
	if ok and type(result) == "table" then
		return result
	end
	local united, union = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:UnionAsync(part, {})
	end)
	local solid = united and type(union) == "table" and union[1] or nil
	if not solid then
		return nil
	end
	ok, result = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:FragmentAsync(solid, points)
	end)
	solid:Destroy()
	if ok and type(result) == "table" then
		return result
	end
	return nil
end

-- Cuts one job and returns its shards, or false. Yields.
local function cut(job)
	local part = job.part
	if not part.Parent then
		return false
	end
	local frame = part.CFrame
	local random = Sites.sequence(job.seed)
	local offsets
	if job.hit then
		offsets = Sites.aroundHit(part.Size, job.count, job.hit, random)
	else
		offsets = Sites.even(part.Size, job.count, random)
	end
	local points = table.create(#offsets)
	for index, offset in ipairs(offsets) do
		points[index] = frame:PointToWorldSpace(offset)
	end

	local fragments = fragment(part, points)
	if not fragments or #fragments < 2 then
		return false
	end
	local shards = table.create(#fragments)
	for _, entry in ipairs(fragments) do
		local template = entry.Instance
		local extents = template.ExtentsCFrame
		table.insert(shards, {
			template = template,
			box = frame:ToObjectSpace(extents),
			size = template.ExtentsSize,
			standOffset = extents:ToObjectSpace(template.CFrame),
		})
	end
	return shards
end

function Shards.prepare(jobs, done)
	local total = #jobs
	if total == 0 then
		done()
		return
	end
	local taken = 0
	local finished = 0
	local function work()
		while taken < total do
			taken += 1
			local job = jobs[taken]
			local ok, shards = pcall(cut, job)
			kept[job.part] = { key = job.key, shards = ok and shards or false }
			finished += 1
		end
		if finished == total and done then
			local callback = done
			done = nil
			callback()
		end
	end
	for _ = 1, math.min(WORKERS, total) do
		task.spawn(work)
	end
end

return Shards

--[[
	Sites  -  the points a part is broken around with Break = "Shards". The engine cuts one shard
	per point: the part of the solid that is nearer to that point than to any other (a Voronoi
	cell). So the number of points is the number of shards, and where the points are thick the
	shards are small. Numbers only, no instances.

	Sites.count(size, pieces) -> how many points a part of `size` gets
	    `pieces` held to Sites.MAX, and to fewer for a part too small to give that many shards
	    of LEAST_VOLUME each. Under 2 the part is not cut.
	Sites.even(size, count, random) -> { Vector3 }
	    anywhere in the part's box: shards of about one size.
	Sites.aroundHit(size, count, hit, random) -> { Vector3 }
	    NEAR_SHARE of the points near `hit`, the rest anywhere: small shards where the part was
	    struck, large ones away from it.
	Sites.hitIn(size, point) -> the point of the part's box nearest to `point`
	Sites.sequence(seed) -> random: numbers from 0 to 1, the same for the same seed
	Points and `hit` are offsets in the part's own space; points keep a little inside the box.
	`random` gives 0 to 1; the same sequence gives the same points. A point that falls outside
	the solid itself (the corner of a ball's box) cuts no shard, so a round part gives a few
	fewer than asked.
]]

local Sites = {}

Sites.MAX = 240
-- The average shard is never smaller than this, in cubic studs: a half-stud cube.
local LEAST_VOLUME = 0.125
-- Points stay within this share of the box, clear of its faces.
local INSET = 0.95
-- aroundHit: the share of the points gathered near the hit, how far from it they reach as a
-- share of the part's longest edge, and how strongly they crowd toward it (under 1 crowds).
local NEAR_SHARE = 0.7
local NEAR_REACH = 0.4
local CROWDING = 0.6

function Sites.sequence(seed)
	local state = seed % 2147483647
	return function()
		state = (state * 48271 + 11) % 2147483647
		return state / 2147483647
	end
end

function Sites.count(size, pieces)
	local wanted = math.floor(math.min(pieces, Sites.MAX))
	local room = math.floor(size.X * size.Y * size.Z / LEAST_VOLUME)
	return math.max(math.min(wanted, room), 0)
end

local function anywhere(size, random)
	return Vector3.new((random() - 0.5) * size.X, (random() - 0.5) * size.Y, (random() - 0.5) * size.Z) * INSET
end

function Sites.even(size, count, random)
	local points = table.create(count)
	for index = 1, count do
		points[index] = anywhere(size, random)
	end
	return points
end

function Sites.hitIn(size, point)
	local half = size / 2
	return Vector3.new(math.clamp(point.X, -half.X, half.X), math.clamp(point.Y, -half.Y, half.Y), math.clamp(point.Z, -half.Z, half.Z))
end

function Sites.aroundHit(size, count, hit, random)
	local points = table.create(count)
	local reach = math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z) * NEAR_REACH
	local near = math.floor(count * NEAR_SHARE)
	for index = 1, count do
		if index > near then
			points[index] = anywhere(size, random)
		else
			local direction = Vector3.new(random() - 0.5, random() - 0.5, random() - 0.5)
			if direction.Magnitude < 1e-4 then
				direction = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
			end
			local offset = hit + direction.Unit * (reach * random() ^ CROWDING)
			points[index] = Sites.hitIn(size, offset) * INSET
		end
	end
	return points
end

return Sites

--[[
	Support  -  which pieces of a Reactor hold each other up, so that a piece left with nothing
	under or beside it can fall. Numbers only, no instances.

	Two pieces are neighbours when their boxes meet face to face: world-axis boxes around each
	piece at rest, no farther apart than a small margin along one axis and overlapping by a good
	part of the smaller box along the other two. Boxes that only meet at an edge or a corner do
	not hold each other. A piece is anchored when the caller says so (Reactor/init:
	something that is not the Reactor lies right under it). A piece is supported when a chain of
	neighbours that are still standing leads from it to a standing anchored piece.

	Support.build(pieces, isAnchored) -> graph, with graph.supported[index] true for every piece
	that is supported while everything stands. A piece that floats from the start (a lamp hung in
	mid-air) is not, and is never made to fall.
	Support.unsupported(graph, isStanding) -> the pieces that were supported at rest, still stand,
	and have lost their last chain to an anchor.
]]

local Support = {}

-- How far apart two boxes may be and still count as touching, in studs.
local TOUCH_MARGIN = 0.15
-- Along the two axes of a shared face, the boxes must overlap by this share of the smaller one.
local FACE_SHARE = 0.25
-- The grid the boxes are sorted into, so that only pieces near each other are compared.
local LEAST_CELL = 2

-- Half the size of the world-axis box around a piece at rest.
function Support.worldHalf(piece)
	local rest = piece.rest
	local half = piece.halfExt
	local right, up, back = rest.XVector, rest.YVector, rest.ZVector
	return Vector3.new(
		math.abs(right.X) * half.X + math.abs(up.X) * half.Y + math.abs(back.X) * half.Z,
		math.abs(right.Y) * half.X + math.abs(up.Y) * half.Y + math.abs(back.Y) * half.Z,
		math.abs(right.Z) * half.X + math.abs(up.Z) * half.Y + math.abs(back.Z) * half.Z
	)
end

-- Along one axis: 2 when the boxes overlap deeply enough to share a face across it, 1 when
-- they at least touch, 0 when they are apart.
local function contact(offset, firstHalf, secondHalf)
	local overlap = firstHalf + secondHalf - math.abs(offset)
	if overlap >= FACE_SHARE * 2 * math.min(firstHalf, secondHalf) then
		return 2
	elseif overlap >= -TOUCH_MARGIN then
		return 1
	end
	return 0
end

-- Face to face: touching along every axis and overlapping deeply along at least two.
function Support.touching(firstCentre, firstHalf, secondCentre, secondHalf)
	local alongX = contact(firstCentre.X - secondCentre.X, firstHalf.X, secondHalf.X)
	local alongY = contact(firstCentre.Y - secondCentre.Y, firstHalf.Y, secondHalf.Y)
	local alongZ = contact(firstCentre.Z - secondCentre.Z, firstHalf.Z, secondHalf.Z)
	if alongX == 0 or alongY == 0 or alongZ == 0 then
		return false
	end
	return alongX + alongY + alongZ >= 5
end

-- Every piece reachable from the standing anchored ones through standing neighbours.
local function reached(graph, isStanding)
	local seen = {}
	local queue = {}
	for index in pairs(graph.anchored) do
		if isStanding(index) then
			seen[index] = true
			table.insert(queue, index)
		end
	end
	local head = 1
	while head <= #queue do
		local index = queue[head]
		head += 1
		for _, neighbour in ipairs(graph.neighbours[index]) do
			if not seen[neighbour] and isStanding(neighbour) then
				seen[neighbour] = true
				table.insert(queue, neighbour)
			end
		end
	end
	return seen
end

function Support.build(pieces, isAnchored)
	local count = #pieces
	local centres = table.create(count)
	local halves = table.create(count)
	local cell = LEAST_CELL
	for index, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		centres[index] = piece.rest.Position
		halves[index] = Support.worldHalf(piece)
		cell = math.max(cell, halves[index].X * 2, halves[index].Y * 2, halves[index].Z * 2)
	end

	-- A box is listed in every cell it reaches into; two boxes are compared once, in the first
	-- cell they share.
	local cells = {}
	local neighbours = table.create(count)
	local paired = {}
	for index = 1, count do
		neighbours[index] = {}
		local centre, half = centres[index], halves[index]
		for x = math.floor((centre.X - half.X - TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell), math.floor((centre.X + half.X + TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell) do
			for y = math.floor((centre.Y - half.Y - TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell), math.floor((centre.Y + half.Y + TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell) do
				for z = math.floor((centre.Z - half.Z - TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell), math.floor((centre.Z + half.Z + TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell) do
					local key = x .. "," .. y .. "," .. z
					local members = cells[key]
					if not members then
						members = {}
						cells[key] = members
					end
					for _, other in ipairs(members) do
						local pair = other * (count + 1) + index
						if not paired[pair] then
							paired[pair] = true
							if Support.touching(centre, half, centres[other], halves[other]) then
								table.insert(neighbours[index], other)
								table.insert(neighbours[other], index)
							end
						end
					end
					table.insert(members, index)
				end
			end
		end
	end

	local anchored = {}
	for index = 1, count do
		if isAnchored(index) then
			anchored[index] = true
		end
	end
	local graph = { neighbours = neighbours, anchored = anchored, supported = {} }
	graph.supported = reached(graph, function()
		return true
	end)
	return graph
end

function Support.unsupported(graph, isStanding)
	local held = reached(graph, isStanding)
	local fallen = {}
	for index in pairs(graph.supported) do
		if not held[index] and isStanding(index) then
			table.insert(fallen, index)
		end
	end
	table.sort(fallen)
	return fallen
end

return Support

--[[
	RegisterEmit Mixin  -  Particle:_registerEmit, the universal pData insertion chokepoint.
	Every EmitX type funnels fresh pData through here: cap check, chain-id stamp, ActiveEmits
	insert, OnHit raycast seed, OnEmit fire. Also stamps the per-play "ghost" token
	(emitCtx._playToken) onto pData so AbsoluteEmitAt's PlayHandle can scope Disable /
	SetTimescale / GetParticles to one play, and inherits that play's live timescale window
	onto new emits without writing _tsOverride attributes to the shared source.

	Split out of Lifecycle.luau to keep that file under the 500-line code cap. Must be applied
	(require(script.RegisterEmit)(Particle)) before any emit runs.
]]

local Events = require(script.Parent.Events)
local Pool = require(script.Parent.Pool)
local LinkCF = require(script.Parent.LinkCF)

return function(Particle)

	-- Register fresh pData: stamp chain id + play token, insert ActiveEmits, seed OnHit raycast, fire OnEmit.
	function Particle:_registerEmit(pData, emitCtx)
		-- Active-particle cap (counts ActiveEmits + linger visuals).
		local cap = self.MAX_ACTIVE_PARTICLES or 1000
		if #self.ActiveEmits + (self._lingerVisualCount or 0) >= cap then
			-- 3D Animate uses LIVE source RT; can't destroy. Clone-Animate (Screen/ImageLabel) destroys.
			local liveRTAnimate = self:_isLiveRTAnimate(pData)
			if pData.IsAnimate and pData._sourceItem then self.ActiveAnimates[pData._sourceItem] = nil end
			-- Emitters create _nestedAlive before registering; flipping it here makes their nested walk a no-op.
			self:_reclaimPData(pData)
			if not liveRTAnimate and pData.VisualPart and pData.VisualPart.Parent then
				-- Cap-reject: route through _releaseOrDestroy so the visual enters the pool.
				self:_releaseOrDestroy(pData, pData.VisualPart)
			end
			return
		end
		-- Root emits with no incoming emitCtx still get a fresh ChainCtx so OnEmit /
		-- OnDeath / OnHit on the same particle share identity (otherwise OnDeath would fire
		-- under a NEW root chain and chain-tracking across lifetime would break).
		pData.EventChainCtx = (emitCtx and emitCtx.ChainCtx) or pData.EventChainCtx or Events.newChainCtx()

		-- Per-play ghost token: tags this particle so PlayHandle can sweep / timescale only
		-- this play. New emits during an active play-timescale window inherit it here, so the
		-- override never has to be written to the shared source item's attributes.
		local token = emitCtx and emitCtx._playToken
		if token then
			pData._playToken = token
			if token.TsOverride ~= nil and token.TsUntil and os.clock() < token.TsUntil then
				pData._tsOverride = token.TsOverride
				pData._tsOverrideUntil = token.TsUntil
			end
		end

		-- Play-scoped authoring survives AnimateLoop cycles (EngineReplay re-reads the source).
		if emitCtx then
			pData._playOverrides = emitCtx.Overrides
			pData._playLink = emitCtx._playLink
		end

		-- Link generation: the pool bumps it on every release, so a recycled clone stops being a
		-- valid link for particles that captured it earlier (LinkCF.isValid).
		-- Force/init reads its first link frame only after this has run.
		if pData.Link then pData._linkGen = Pool.linkGen(pData.Link) end
		if emitCtx and emitCtx._parentAlive ~= nil then pData._nestedDriven = true end
		LinkCF.captureEmitFrame(pData)
		table.insert(self.ActiveEmits, pData)
		if pData.Events and pData.Events.OnHit then
			pData.LastHitCheckPos = Events.getWorldPosition(pData)
			pData.HitParams = Events.makeHitParams(pData)
			pData._hitFired = false
		end
		if pData.Events and pData.Events.OnEmit then
			-- Build payload explicitly so EmitIndex (per-burst index) reaches user scripts.
			-- Events.fire's nil-payload fallback can't synthesize EmitIndex because it
			-- doesn't see emitCtx.
			local payload = Events.makePayload(self, pData, "OnEmit", emitCtx)
			Events.fire(self, pData, "OnEmit", pData.EventChainCtx, payload)
		end
	end

end

--[[
	Rocks Mixin  -  Emit + Animate + Update for debris bursts.

	FULLY PREDETERMINED playback (Rocks/Trajectory.luau) in edit AND running
	games: the complete path  -  arcs, bounces, roll-out, exact rest pose  -  is
	computed once at emit with ~a dozen raycasts per chunk; every frame just
	evaluates pose(t) and BulkMoveTo's. Nothing integrates, so jitter and
	unpredicted end poses are impossible, Timescale (including reverse) replays
	the path exactly, and the game's physics engine never touches the chunks.

	Path building is spread over frames (TRAJ_BUILD_BUDGET chunks per frame); a chunk flies a
	ballistic placeholder until its own path lands, so a 32-chunk burst never spikes one frame.

	OnHit fires from the precomputed first impact (once per burst, or per chunk with HitPerChunk). The generic Events.afterUpdate
	raycast must NOT run here: the Model pivot is the LIVE bounding-box center
	(no PrimaryPart), so it moves with the chunks — pData._ownsOnHit gates it off
	(set in Rocks/PDataBuilder; consumer check at the top of Events.afterUpdate).
]]

local GraphMod = require(script.Parent.Graph)
local RangeMod = require(script.Parent.Range)
local Pool = require(script.Parent.Pool)
local EventsMod = require(script.Parent.Events)
local NestedEmit = require(script.Parent.NestedEmit)
local ParticlesMod = require(script.Parent.Particles)
local Constants = require(script.Parent.PartConstants)
local Trajectory = require(script.Trajectory)
local PDataBuilder = require(script.PDataBuilder)

local MAX_CHUNKS = 32
-- Chunk paths built per frame; each build costs up to ~18 raycasts.
local TRAJ_BUILD_BUDGET = 8
local FAR_CFRAME = CFrame.new(1e9, 1e9, 1e9)
-- Rested chunks sink through the floor over the last 15% of life (SinkOut).
local SINK_START = 0.85

-- Weak-keyed by burst Model so rig buffers survive pool release/acquire cycles.
local Rigs = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

return function(Particle)

-- Rocks discriminator; shared by init.luau Emit dispatch + Lifecycle EmitAnimate dispatch.
function Particle._isRocks(item)
	return item:IsA("BasePart") and item:GetAttribute("IsRocks") == true
end

-- One chunk part cloned from the RT. copyBare strips Transformed children (nested
-- source Part-Icles fire once per BURST via NestedEmit.walk, never per chunk).
-- Chunks stay ANCHORED for life  -  trajectory playback drives their CFrames.
local function buildChunk(rt)
	local chunk = Pool.copyBare(rt)
	chunk.Anchored = true
	chunk.CanCollide = false
	chunk.CanQuery = false
	chunk.CanTouch = false
	chunk.Massless = false
	chunk.Locked = true
	chunk.Archivable = false
	chunk.CastShadow = true
	chunk.Transparency = 0
	local decal = chunk:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Decal") or chunk:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Texture")
	return chunk, decal
end

local function chunkCapFor(data)
	return math.clamp(math.floor((data.ChunkCount and data.ChunkCount.Max or 10) + 0.5), 1, MAX_CHUNKS)
end

local function buildRig(data)
	local cap = chunkCapFor(data)
	local model = Instance.new("Model")
	model.Name = "RockBurst"
	model.Archivable = false
	local rig = {
		chunkCap = cap,
		parts = table.create(cap),
		decals = table.create(cap),
		baseSize = table.create(cap),
		halfExt = table.create(cap),
		bounciness = table.create(cap),
		gravity = table.create(cap),
		friction = table.create(cap),
		-- Trajectory seeds + playback buffers.
		launchVel = table.create(cap),
		launchAng = table.create(cap),
		spawnPos = table.create(cap),
		spawnRot = table.create(cap),
		trajs = table.create(cap),
		touched = table.create(cap),
		hitDone = table.create(cap),
		writeCFs = table.create(cap),
	}
	for i = 1, cap do
		local chunk, decal = buildChunk(data.RenderTemplate)
		chunk.Name = "Chunk" .. i
		chunk.CFrame = FAR_CFRAME
		chunk.Parent = model
		rig.parts[i] = chunk
		rig.decals[i] = decal
		rig.baseSize[i] = chunk.Size
		rig.writeCFs[i] = FAR_CFRAME
	end
	Rigs[model] = rig
	return model, rig
end

-- Pool acquire with defensive rig re-check (foreign / layout-drifted / engine-
-- destroyed-chunk models rebuild).
local function acquireRocks(data)
	local expected = chunkCapFor(data)
	if data.Pool ~= false then
		local model = Pool.acquire(data.RenderTemplate, "Rocks")
		if model then
			local rig = Rigs[model]
			if rig and rig.chunkCap == expected and rig.parts[1] and rig.parts[1].Parent == model then
				model:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
				return model, rig
			end
			pcall(function() model:Destroy() end)
		end
	end
	local model, rig = buildRig(data)
	model:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	return model, rig
end

-- Step-gated visual write: transparency/color/brightness on every chunk + decal,
-- Scale graph multiplies baseSize.
local function writeVisuals(pData, t)
	local graphs, seeds = pData.Graphs, pData.Seeds
	local trans = graphs.Transparency and GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(t, graphs.Transparency, seeds.Transparency) or 0
	if pData.SkipTransparency then trans = pData._curTrans or trans end
	local bright = graphs.Brightness and GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(t, graphs.Brightness, seeds.Brightness) or 1
	local color
	if graphs.Color and not pData.SkipColor then
		local c = GraphMod.QueryColorPointWithTime(t, graphs.Color)
		color = Color3.new(math.min(c.R * bright, 1), math.min(c.G * bright, 1), math.min(c.B * bright, 1))
	end
	local scale = graphs.Scale and GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(t, graphs.Scale, seeds.Scale)
	local rig = pData._rig
	local scaleChanged = scale and scale ~= pData._curScale
	if scale then pData._curScale = scale end
	pData._curTrans = trans
	for i = 1, rig.chunkCap do
		local chunk = rig.parts[i]
		chunk.Transparency = trans
		if color then chunk.Color = color end
		local decal = rig.decals[i]
		if decal then
			decal.Transparency = trans
			if color then decal.Color3 = color end
		end
		if scaleChanged then
			chunk.Size = rig.baseSize[i] * math.max(scale, 0.01)
		end
	end
end

-- Edit-path raycast params: makeHitParams filter pattern (source/RT/EmitParent/
-- user OnHit cfg) + both engine folders by ancestry + RespectCanCollide so rocks
-- pass through non-collidable decoration.
local function buildRockParams(self, pData)
	local p = EventsMod.makeHitParams(pData)
	p.RespectCanCollide = true
	pcall(function()
		p:AddToFilter(self:GetFolder())
		p:AddToFilter(self:GetPoolFolder())
	end)
	pData._rockParams = p
	pData._raycastFn = function(origin, disp)
		return workspace:Raycast(origin, disp, p)
	end
end

-- Build the next `budget` chunk paths (all raycast cost lives here). Running first-impact /
-- rest accumulators finalize once every chunk is built; until then the write gate stays open.
local function buildTrajectories(pData, budget)
	local rig = pData._rig
	local rayFn = pData._raycastFn
	local scale = pData._curScale or 1
	local first = pData._trajBuilt + 1
	local last = math.min(pData._chunkCount, pData._trajBuilt + budget)
	for i = first, last do
		local traj = Trajectory.build(rig.spawnPos[i], rig.launchVel[i], rig.spawnRot[i], rig.launchAng[i],
			rig.halfExt[i], scale, rig.gravity[i], rig.bounciness[i], rig.friction[i], rayFn)
		rig.trajs[i] = traj
		if traj.impactT and traj.impactT < pData._firstImpactT then
			pData._firstImpactT = traj.impactT
			pData._firstHitInfo = traj.hit
		end
		-- A chunk that never rests (no ground in reach) must keep the write gate
		-- open for its whole life; latching at the max FINITE rest would freeze it
		-- mid-air and snap it far away when the sink phase re-opens the gate.
		if traj.restT == math.huge then
			pData._trajAnyEndless = true
		elseif traj.restT > pData._trajMaxRest then
			pData._trajMaxRest = traj.restT
		end
	end
	pData._trajBuilt = last
	if last >= pData._chunkCount then
		pData._maxRestT = (pData._trajMaxRest > 0 and not pData._trajAnyEndless) and pData._trajMaxRest or math.huge
	end
end

-- Per-burst path setup, shared by Emit / Animate / loop refresh: every chunk starts on a
-- ballistic placeholder, the first budget of real paths lands now, Update builds the rest.
local function startPhysics(self, pData)
	buildRockParams(self, pData)
	local rig = pData._rig
	pData._trajBuilt = 0
	pData._firstImpactT = math.huge
	pData._firstHitInfo = nil
	pData._trajMaxRest = 0
	pData._trajAnyEndless = false
	pData._maxRestT = math.huge
	pData._restWritten = false
	pData._hitsPending = pData._hitPerChunk and pData._chunkCount or 0
	for i = 1, pData._chunkCount do
		rig.trajs[i] = Trajectory.ballistic(rig.spawnPos[i], rig.launchVel[i], rig.spawnRot[i], rig.launchAng[i])
		rig.hitDone[i] = false
	end
	buildTrajectories(pData, TRAJ_BUILD_BUDGET)
end

local function fireChunkHit(self, pData, hit)
	local payload = EventsMod.makePayload(self, pData, "OnHit", nil)
	payload.HitInstance = hit.Instance
	payload.Other = hit.Instance
	payload.HitPosition = hit.Position
	payload.HitNormal = hit.Normal
	EventsMod.fire(self, pData, "OnHit", pData.EventChainCtx, payload)
end

-- Spawn one debris burst.
function Particle:EmitRocks(item, link, emitCtx)
	if not item or not item.Parent then return end
	local data = self:GetEmitData(item, emitCtx)
	if not data or not data.RenderTemplate then return end

	local lifeTime = RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Lifetime)
	if lifeTime <= 0 then lifeTime = 0.001 end

	local model, rig = acquireRocks(data)
	local pData = PDataBuilder.build(item, data, model, rig, lifeTime, emitCtx, link)

	Particle._seedTsOverride(pData, item)
	if data.Pool ~= false then
		pData._sourceRT, pData._poolKind = data.RenderTemplate, "Rocks"
	end

	writeVisuals(pData, 0)
	model.Parent = data.EmitParent or self:GetFolder()
	startPhysics(self, pData)
	Pool.restoreTrails(model, "Rocks")
	ParticlesMod.EnableEmit(model, self:_makeAliveCheck())

	pData._nestedAlive = { true }
	self:_registerEmit(pData, emitCtx)
	NestedEmit.walk(self, data.RenderTemplate, model, pData._nestedAlive, emitCtx)
end

-- Animate mode: singleton looping burst per source (fresh rig, never pooled).
function Particle:EmitRocksAnimate(item, link, emitCtx)
	if not item or not item.Parent then return end
	if self.ActiveAnimates[item] then return end
	local data = self:GetEmitData(item, emitCtx)
	if not data or not data.RenderTemplate then return end

	local lifeTime = RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Lifetime)
	if lifeTime <= 0 then lifeTime = 0.001 end

	local model, rig = buildRig(data)
	model:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	local pData = PDataBuilder.build(item, data, model, rig, lifeTime, emitCtx, link)
	pData.IsAnimate = true
	pData.AnimateItem = item
	pData._animateLink = link

	Particle._seedTsOverride(pData, item)
	writeVisuals(pData, 0)
	model.Parent = data.EmitParent or self:GetFolder()
	startPhysics(self, pData)
	ParticlesMod.EnableEmit(model, self:_makeAliveCheck())

	pData._nestedAlive = { true }
	self.ActiveAnimates[item] = pData
	self:_registerEmit(pData, emitCtx)
	NestedEmit.walk(self, data.RenderTemplate, model, pData._nestedAlive, emitCtx)
end

-- Per-frame update: evaluate the predetermined paths at effective time (any
-- Timescale, any direction) + one BulkMoveTo; idles once everything is at rest.
function Particle:UpdateRocks(pData, dt, currentTime)
	-- Signed-reverse timescale header: see Lightning/init.luau UpdateLightning.
	local real_i = math.min(math.max((currentTime - pData.StartTime) / pData.LifeTime, 0), 1)
	local ts
	if pData._tsOverride ~= nil and currentTime < (pData._tsOverrideUntil or 0) then
		ts = pData._tsOverride
	else
		ts = pData.Graphs.Timescale and GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(real_i, pData.Graphs.Timescale, pData.Seeds.Timescale) or 1
	end
	local dtTs = dt * ts
	local lifeTime = pData.LifeTime
	local newEff = (pData._effectiveElapsed or 0) + (pData._timeFrozen and 0 or dtTs)
	if newEff < 0 then newEff = 0 end
	if newEff > lifeTime then newEff = lifeTime end
	pData._effectiveElapsed = newEff

	local model = pData.VisualPart
	if not model or not model.Parent then return true end
	if pData.TotalKeyFrames <= 0 then return true end
	local isDying = real_i >= 1 and (newEff >= lifeTime or newEff <= 0)

	if not isDying then
		local rig = pData._rig
		if pData._trajBuilt < pData._chunkCount then buildTrajectories(pData, TRAJ_BUILD_BUDGET) end
		local sinkPhase = pData._sinkOut and (newEff / lifeTime) > SINK_START
		if newEff < pData._maxRestT or sinkPhase or not pData._restWritten then
			local sinkEase = 0
			if sinkPhase then
				local e = ((newEff / lifeTime) - SINK_START) / (1 - SINK_START)
				sinkEase = e * e
			end
			for i = 1, pData._chunkCount do
				local traj = rig.trajs[i]
				if traj then
					local cf = Trajectory.evaluate(traj, newEff, rig.gravity[i])
					if sinkEase > 0 and newEff > traj.restT then
						-- Full burial along the rest surface normal: largest dimension
						-- (scaled) × 1.5 clears the surface with margin.
						local sz = rig.baseSize[i]
						local depth = math.max(sz.X, sz.Y, sz.Z) * math.max(pData._curScale or 1, 0.01) * 1.5
						cf = cf.Rotation + (cf.Position - (traj.restNormal or Vector3.yAxis) * (depth * sinkEase))
					end
					rig.writeCFs[i] = cf
					-- InheritFloor lands the moment the path says it does.
					if pData._inheritFloor and not rig.touched[i] and traj.impactT and newEff >= traj.impactT and traj.hit then
						rig.touched[i] = true
						local part = rig.parts[i]
						pcall(function()
							part.Material = traj.hit.Instance.Material
							part.Color = traj.hit.Instance.Color
						end)
						pData.SkipColor = true
					end
				end
			end
			workspace:BulkMoveTo(rig.parts, rig.writeCFs, Enum.BulkMoveMode.FireCFrameChanged)
			-- One flush past rest, then idle until sink or reversed time.
			pData._restWritten = newEff >= pData._maxRestT and not sinkPhase
		end
		-- OnHit from the precomputed impacts: once per burst at the earliest, or per chunk.
		if pData.Events and pData.Events.OnHit then
			if pData._hitPerChunk then
				if pData._hitsPending > 0 then
					for i = 1, pData._chunkCount do
						local traj = rig.trajs[i]
						if not rig.hitDone[i] and traj.impactT and traj.hit and newEff >= traj.impactT then
							rig.hitDone[i] = true
							pData._hitsPending -= 1
							fireChunkHit(self, pData, traj.hit)
						end
					end
				end
			elseif not pData._hitFired and pData._trajBuilt >= pData._chunkCount
				and pData._firstHitInfo and newEff >= pData._firstImpactT then
				pData._hitFired = true
				fireChunkHit(self, pData, pData._firstHitInfo)
			end
		end
	end

	local targetStep = math.floor(math.min(math.max(newEff / lifeTime, 0), 1) * pData.TotalKeyFrames)
	if targetStep ~= pData.CurrentStep then
		pData.CurrentStep = targetStep
		writeVisuals(pData, targetStep / pData.TotalKeyFrames)
	end

	return isDying
end

-- AnimateLoop per-cycle refresh (EngineReplay dispatch): re-roll every chunk from
-- the source's CURRENT pose, rebuild paths, restart physics; rebuild the rig on
-- layout change.
function Particle:_refreshRocksAnimate(pData, freshData)
	-- Generic replay assigns pData.Link from freshData; Rocks never links post-emit.
	pData.Link = nil
	pData._sinkOut = freshData.SinkOut ~= false
	pData._inheritFloor = freshData.InheritFloor == true
	pData._hitPerChunk = freshData.HitPerChunk == true
	pData._hitFired = false
	pData.SkipColor = nil

	local expected = chunkCapFor(freshData)
	if expected ~= pData._rig.chunkCap and freshData.RenderTemplate then
		local oldModel = pData.VisualPart
		local parent = oldModel and oldModel.Parent
		local model, rig = buildRig(freshData)
		model:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
		pData.VisualPart = model
		pData._rig = rig
		model.Parent = parent or self:GetFolder()
		if oldModel then pcall(function() oldModel:Destroy() end) end
	end
